newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran calls for Indian Ocean security organisation.
newsitem.headline: Iran calls for Indian Ocean security organisation.

text.p: Iran's President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Sunday called for a regional organisation to promote security and cooperation in the Indian Ocean, saying Iran could play an important role.

"The strategic importance and broadness of the Indian Ocean region necessitates that regional states join hands to preserve security and boost cooperation by setting up a powerful forum," Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said to open an international conference on the Indian Ocean community.
Rafsanjani, quoted by official radio, said Iran was a "strong link in the chain" of Indian Ocean littoral states. "Iran is a reliable anchor for the ship of peace in the region," he added.
The three-day conference in Tehran is attended by officials from about 30 regional countries.
Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati told delegates the Indian Ocean area, home to over 1.5 billion people, clearly felt the lack of a regional body.

"Cooperation in the Indian Ocean is not only a proper ground for economic relations but also...ultimately it is a powerful element in the service of peace and security regionally as well as internationally," he said.
Among participants were officials from India, Pakistan, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Madagascar, Oman, Kenya, Zimbabwe, Turkey, Georgia, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan and Brunei.
